objective: Quantify how international tourists from different continents rate 17 attraction types in Indonesia (destination), expressed as mean transaction Rating per (AttractionType, Continent) group, then annotate every row with Indonesia's macro context (GDP per capita, Henley visa-free score) so that rating differences can be interpreted against destination-level macro conditions.

data_inventory.role: fact table - supplies the Rating being averaged
dimension - maps reviewer to continent of origin (note misspelling 'ContenentId')
decode ContenentId -> continent label; id 0 = '-' placeholder and is unused by User
dimension - maps attraction to its type id

data_inventory.fields_note: column names carry odd characters/units, e.g. 'GDP ($ per capita)'; Country must be .str.strip() before matching
data_inventory.role: macro source for Country_GDP_per_Capita (Indonesia = 3200 USD per capita, World-Bank ~2006 snapshot)
macro source for Visa_Free_Score (Indonesia -> Rank 66, Visa_Free_Score 74)

evaluation_units.reason_for_78: 7 combos have zero reviews (6 Africa-type combos + Spas/America) and are therefore absent, not zero-filled

pipeline_steps.name: load
pipeline_steps.detail: Read the 5 xlsx sheets with xlsx_reader.read_xlsx (pure-python zip/XML parser, no openpyxl dependency) and the 2 CSVs with pandas; cast Rating/Ids to int.

pipeline_steps.name: conform keys
pipeline_steps.detail: Strip whitespace on both country columns; rename Transaction.AttractionId -> Item.AttractionId; keep User.ContenentId spelling as-is.

pipeline_steps.name: build fact view
pipeline_steps.detail: Transaction --(UserId)--> User --(ContenentId)--> Continent gives Continent; Transaction --(AttractionId)--> Item --(AttractionTypeId)--> Type gives AttractionType. Inner-join chain; expect 0% row loss (verified).

pipeline_steps.name: aggregate
pipeline_steps.detail: Avg_Rating = mean(Rating) grouped by (AttractionType, Continent); round to 4 decimals; also keep n_reviews internally for the reliability flag.

pipeline_steps.name: attach macro
pipeline_steps.detail: Look up 'Indonesia' in both macro tables and broadcast the two scalars onto every row (left-join on a constant destination key).

pipeline_steps.name: order & write
pipeline_steps.detail: Sort by AttractionType then Continent for reproducibility; write output.csv with exactly the 5 required columns; UTF-8, no index.

Country_GDP_per_Capita.source: countries of the world.csv -> 'GDP ($ per capita)'

Visa_Free_Score.comment: constant across rows; measures outbound visa-free access of the Indonesian passport, i.e. demand-side/mobility context - NOT visa openness of Indonesia toward inbound tourists

validation_checks.expected: 78 rows; 85-78=7 missing combos all have zero transactions

analysis_angle_for_interpretation: Cross-continent variance per attraction type: which types are polarising (large spread across continents) vs universally liked.

Continent marginal means (weighted): Australia & Oceania 4.2124 > America 4.1634 > Asia 4.1557 > Europe 4.1001 > Africa 4.088 - spread ~0.12, small relative to type-level spread, so attraction type dominates continent effects.
Type marginal means: Water Parks 4.65, Spas 4.57, Caverns & Caves 4.50, National Parks 4.42 top; lowest types around 3.3-3.9.

Macro linkage: with GDP per capita 3200 USD and Henley score 74 (Rank 66), Indonesia sits in the mid-tier of both development and outbound mobility; the macro columns are contextual constants, so they support narrative interpretation (price/value, accessibility, infrastructure maturity) rather than statistical variation within this table.
risks_and_caveats: Both macro columns are constant -> they cannot explain within-table variance; any correlation with Avg_Rating is structurally zero. Treat them as annotation only.
Sparse groups (n<5, 8 groups) produce unstable means (e.g. min 3.3333 likely from a 3-review group); interpret with review counts.
'GDP ($ per capita)' in countries of the world.csv is an old (mid-2000s) snapshot and country names have trailing spaces; wrong matching would silently produce NaN.
VisitMode/VisitYear/VisitMonth not required by the deliverable but available for robustness slicing (e.g. exclude low-review masks) if a deeper node needs it.
Africa is heavily under-represented (593 reviewers) so its extremes carry the most noise.
